about.heading: Hello, I'm Artyom.
about.headingMuted: Product Designer for complex digital products.
paragraphs: My journey began with architecture. I wanted to design buildings, but over time I realized that creating digital spaces where people solve real problems is much more interesting.

I have been working in interface design for over five years. For the last two years, I have been focused on digital services for the construction industry: designing complex user scenarios, analytical systems, and tools for handling large volumes of data.
I enjoy finding order in complexity. Understanding processes, asking questions, eliminating the unnecessary, and turning convoluted logic into clear interfaces.
Currently, I am actively exploring AI capabilities, experimenting with new tools, and looking for ways to make the process of creating digital products faster and more efficient.

values.title: Systems Thinking
values.body: I look at the product as a whole, considering the relationships between elements, users, and processes.

values.title: Simplicity in Complexity
values.body: I transform complex processes into clear and user-friendly interfaces, removing everything unnecessary.

values.title: Meaningful Design
values.body: Every decision I make has a purpose and should bring real benefits to users and the business.

values.title: Continuous Development
values.body: I study new technologies, experiment, and seek more effective ways to solve problems.

jobs.body:
Designed and built a design system from scratch for Moscow's Urban Development Complex, establishing a unified standard across its digital services.

Design complex digital products and workflows, transforming technical requirements into intuitive, scalable interfaces.

Designed user-centered interfaces for B2B and B2C digital products, focusing on usability, functionality, and visual consistency.

Translated complex requirements into intuitive user flows, interactive prototypes, and scalable UI solutions.

Designed presentations and visual materials for government and urban development projects, making complex information clear and accessible.

Created infographics, data visualizations, and structured layouts to communicate key ideas effectively.

Designed responsive websites and landing pages, combining usability with modern visual design.

Created custom illustrations and graphic assets to establish a consistent visual identity across digital experiences.

projects.title: CRM platform for managing room bookings
projects.summary: CRM for space operators: managing rooms, occupancy calendar, and analytics, all integrated into one workflow instead of dozens of spreadsheets and chats.

brief.title: Summary
brief.text: If you're too lazy to read and scroll

sections.heading: Managing spaces in one system
paragraphs: The operator manages dozens of spaces across several buildings. Previously, bookings were handled through spreadsheets and correspondence, leading to scheduling conflicts, fragmented data, and inefficient workflows. Frequent staff turnover added another challenge: new administrators required time-consuming training to handle everyday tasks.

insights.heading: The Impact
paragraphs: A unified CRM was designed to bring bookings, calendars, resource management, and analytics into one place. Simplified workflows, intuitive navigation, and clear visual feedback were introduced to reduce manual work, prevent errors, and help new employees get started with minimal training.

sections.heading: Manual bookings and a steep learning curve
paragraphs: Information about spaces, clients, and requests was scattered across different sources. During calls, administrators had to manually check availability, clarify booking details, and monitor scheduling conflicts.
Frequent staff turnover made the situation worse. Each new employee needed training to understand the booking process, increasing operational costs and slowing down daily work.

points.title: Scheduling conflicts
points.text: Rooms could be booked for overlapping times due to manual checks.

points.title: Fragmented data
points.text: Information about clients, spaces, and requests was spread across multiple sources.

points.title: Limited visibility
points.text: Administrators had to manually check occupancy and availability across buildings.

points.title: Complex approvals
points.text: Different employees participated in the same process but did not have a unified workspace.

sections.heading: First, understand the logic, then design the interface.
paragraphs: I started by analyzing booking scenarios, user roles, and existing interface solutions. It was important to determine what data was needed at each stage and where errors might occur.
I focused primarily on calendars, booking statuses, resource management, and access control.

sections.heading: One booking connects all data
paragraphs: I mapped out the sequence of actions from the incoming call to the booking confirmation. I focused on what data the administrator needs at each stage, where errors occur, and what actions can be simplified.

insights.heading: Dashboard — everything that needs attention
paragraphs: The administrator opens the day and immediately understands: what is confirmed, what is awaiting a decision, where conflicts are brewing. The dashboard answers questions before they are even asked.

insights.heading: Visibility of occupancy
paragraphs: All rooms on one timeline. Overlaps are visible before they become a problem, and available slots are immediately apparent, without mental calculations.

insights.heading: A personalized view for everyone
paragraphs: The administrator, manager, and leader see the system from their own perspective. Permissions define not only access but also what a person sees first — and what they don’t need to see at all.

insights.heading: Booking without unnecessary steps
paragraphs: All data, checks, and additional services are consolidated into one scenario to facilitate quick and error-free bookings.

sections.heading: A good interface helps focus on the client, not the system.
paragraphs: The main goal was to reduce the number of manual checks and switches between sections. The administrator should quickly find the necessary information and book without losing the context of the conversation.

projects.title: Construction tender management, all in one place
projects.summary: A B2B platform designed to connect construction companies and contractors, bringing tender management, applications, and contractor selection into one unified workspace.

brief.title: Summary
brief.text: If you're too lazy to read and scroll

sections.heading: Building a tender platform from scratch
paragraphs: The project started with a business goal rather than an existing product to redesign. I was responsible for translating requirements into a complete user experience, defining the information architecture, user roles, and key workflows.
The main challenge was to make a complex, multi-stage tender process clear and manageable for everyone involved.

insights.heading: The Outcome
paragraphs: A complete product experience was designed, including tender management, contractor profiles, applications, shortlisting, and selection workflows.
The platform was structured around different user roles, with clear navigation, transparent statuses, and tools for evaluating contractors.

sections.heading: Turning a complex process into a simple workflow
paragraphs: With no existing product to redesign, the main challenge was to translate business requirements into a clear and scalable digital experience.
The platform needed to support multiple user roles, complex tender workflows, and large amounts of contractor data — without making everyday tasks unnecessarily complicated.

points.title: Multiple user roles
points.text: Different participants needed tailored workflows, permissions, and interfaces.

points.title: Complex tender lifecycle
points.text: Every stage, from tender creation to winner selection, required clear actions and statuses.

points.title: Contractor evaluation
points.text: Organizers needed an efficient way to review applications, compare candidates, and create shortlists.

points.title: Data & verification
points.text: Company information and external verification sources needed to be accessible within the evaluation process.

insights.heading: End-to-End Tender Workflow
paragraphs: Designed the entire tender lifecycle, from creating and publishing a tender to reviewing applications and selecting a winner. Clear stages, statuses, and actions help users navigate the process and understand what happens next.

insights.heading: Role-Based Experience
paragraphs: Designed tailored experiences for tender organizers and contractors, giving each role access to relevant tools and workflows. This keeps the interface focused on users' tasks without unnecessary complexity.

insights.heading: Contractor Evaluation
paragraphs: Created a structured evaluation process that helps organizers review applications, compare contractors, verify company information, and build shortlists. All the information needed to make a decision is accessible within a single workflow.

sections.heading: From requirements to a cohesive product
paragraphs: Designing this platform from scratch required more than creating interfaces. The key challenge was to structure complex business processes into a clear, consistent experience for different user roles.
The result is a scalable product design that connects tender management, contractor evaluation, and decision-making into one unified workflow.
